content: styrened has three separate systems touching hub/network settings: (1) core-config.yaml reticulum/config for TCP interfaces, (2) HubConnection for LXMF propagation destination tracking, (3) TUI first-run config generator with hardcoded template

The LXMF hub destination hash (6fc8bf22aa293588c9bf8d7488102e95) is hardcoded and separate from TCP transport interfaces - HubConnection.connect() uses RNS.Transport.has_path()/request_path() for LXMF store-and-forward, not for establishing TCP connections
RNS TCPClientInterface peers are defined in core-config.yaml under reticulum.interfaces.peers, then generate_rns_config() writes them to ~/.reticulum/config which RNS reads at startup

Planned Network tab scope: peer list management (add/remove/edit TCPClientInterface entries), AutoInterface on/off toggle, transport mode (standalone/shared, enable_transport), all writing back to core-config.yaml and regenerating ~/.reticulum/config
get_profile_defaults() seeds config.reticulum.interfaces.peers with rns.styrene.io:4242 as a TCPClientInterface stanza
styrened uses async-first architecture with asyncio event loop, periodic tasks for announces and cleanup
CI/CD runs on Argo Workflows on brutus K3s cluster, triggered by Argo Events GitHub webhooks. GitHub Actions removed.

Settings screen Network tab redesign is in progress: removing hub selector/KNOWN_HUBS/STYRENE_HUB_ADDRESS UI, replacing with TCPClientInterface peer manager (add/remove/edit), AutoInterface toggle, transport mode (DeploymentMode enum), and server interface config. Save writes both core-config.yaml and regenerates ~/.reticulum/config.

CoreConfig model includes DeploymentMode enum (STANDALONE, HUB, etc.), PeerConfig (host, port, name), ServerInterfaceConfig (enabled, listen_ip, port), and InterfaceConfig (peers list, auto bool, server) under config.reticulum.interfaces
Config validation via validate_core_config() returns errors with field names — validates peer host non-empty, port in valid range, and hub mode requiring server or peer interfaces
Config serialization uses _serialize_config() which converts CoreConfig to dict; PeerConfig entries without a name omit the name key from serialized output

Settings screen Network tab now has 5 panels: TRANSPORT (mode, enable_transport, announce_interval), PEERS (dynamic add/remove TCPClientInterface rows), LOCAL DISCOVERY (AutoInterface toggle), SERVER (TCPServerInterface enable/IP/port), BATMAN-ADV MESH (existing mesh settings)
Settings save now persists network config to both core-config.yaml (via save_core_config) AND regenerates ~/.reticulum/config (via generate_rns_config + write_text) so RNS picks up changes on restart
KNOWN_HUBS dict, hub_select widget, custom hub address input, and hub announce interval have been removed from the settings screen - replaced by the interface manager panels

The LXMF hub address, hub selector (KNOWN_HUBS), and hub_announce_interval fields have been removed from the TUI settings screen as part of the Network tab redesign. Hub/propagation is handled separately from the interface manager.
Peer list in Network tab now has column headers (Name/Host/Port) rendered as a .peer-header-row of Static widgets with .peer-header CSS class above the dynamic peer rows

styrene --upgrade CLI runs pipx upgrade styrene (or pip install --upgrade) then pkill -f styrened daemon. styrene --reset backs up configs as .bak, regenerates core-config.yaml and ~/.reticulum/config from defaults, and kills daemon.

TUI app's _show_upgrade_screen callback calls _restart_tui() which uses os.execvp to re-exec the process. _restart_tui() finds the styrene entry point (argv0 or shutil.which), calls self.exit(), then registers atexit handler to exec after Textual teardown.

UpgradeScreen upgrade flow: _build_upgrade_cmd() detects pipx vs pip and uses --upgrade-strategy=eager to force transitive dep upgrades. _do_upgrade() runs subprocess in @work thread with 120s timeout, streams output to Log widget, then kills daemon via pkill. Dismiss returns bool to app callback.

Settings screen tab navigation uses [ and ] screen-level keyboard bindings that delegate to TabbedContent.action_previous/next_tab, bypassing arrow key consumption by Input widgets inside tab panes (v0.10.46)

UpgradeScreen._build_upgrade_cmd() passes --upgrade-strategy=eager for both pipx and pip paths. For pipx, uses '--pip-args=--upgrade-strategy=eager' as single combined argument (fixed from two separate args that pipx couldn't parse).

RNS interfaces have .online attribute for connection status, accessible via RNS.Transport.interfaces — rns_service._log_interface_status() and _last_interface_states dict track UP/DOWN state changes at runtime

TUI has 19+ files with inline CSS (CSS = or DEFAULT_CSS =): screens (upgrade, contacts, conversation, exploration, inbox, provision, confirm_flash, mesh_device_detail) and widgets (chat_widget, config_form, activity_feed, node_info_panel, hardware_panel, message_bubble, image_preview, uptime_panel, highlighted_panel, page_browser, forge_log). Main theme CSS lives in imperial_crt.tcss.

Textual ColorSystem has limited built-in theme variables (primary, secondary, warning, error, success, accent, foreground, background, surface, panel, boost, text_alpha). Custom variables are added via the 'variables' dict parameter. styrene_brand.py adds: border, border-blurred, block-cursor-*, footer-*, input-*, scrollbar*, and text-muted.

Settings screen uses Switch (not Checkbox) for all toggles as of v0.10.52. Switch renders as a sliding toggle. CSS class .setting-checkbox styles it borderless/transparent/compact. Save handler queries Switch widgets, not Checkbox. Tests use Switch import.

Custom Textual theme variable $text-muted added to styrene_brand.py ColorSystem variables dict, mapped to STYRENE_DARK['muted_foreground'] (#9ca3af) — provides readable muted text color for descriptions and headers. Used in imperial_crt.tcss for .setting-description and .peer-header.

TUI scrollbar architecture (v0.10.54): Screen-level global scrollbar rules (scrollbar-background:$surface, scrollbar-color:$border, size:1). Blanket transparent background rule for VerticalScroll/ScrollableContainer/RichLog/Log/TextArea. Individual widgets (ActivityFeed, ForgeLog, ChatWidget) have explicit scrollbar styling in DEFAULT_CSS. All scrollable containers must set background+scrollbar-track+scrollbar-thumb.

styrene-pypi sync-version.yml now builds and publishes to PyPI directly (not via release event cascade). GITHUB_TOKEN-created releases cannot trigger other workflows (GitHub anti-cascade). The workflow: detect new styrened on PyPI → bump pyproject.toml → commit+tag → build wheel → publish to PyPI → create GitHub release. Cron hourly + repository_dispatch from Argo.
Local PyPI publish path added: justfile 'publish' recipe runs .venv/bin/python -m build + .venv/bin/python -m twine upload dist/* for immediate availability instead of waiting for Argo CI

Argo release-build.yaml uses twine upload --skip-existing, so local pre-publishing via 'just publish' doesn't break the Argo pipeline — it silently skips the already-uploaded wheel and continues to OCI build and GitHub Release steps

RNS announce callback chain is being investigated to determine if the receiving interface name is available in announce handlers — needed for correlating discovered devices to their source hub/peer for hierarchical display

RNS announce handler callback signature is fixed at 3-5 params (destination_hash, announced_identity, app_data, announce_packet_hash, is_path_response) — receiving interface is NOT passed to handlers. However, RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5] stores the receiving_interface object post-announce, with .name attribute matching config stanza name.

RNS.Transport dispatches announce handlers via inspect.signature() parameter count detection (3, 4, or 5 params) and runs each handler in a separate daemon thread via threading.Thread(target=job, daemon=True).start()

NodeStore SQLite schema uses ALTER TABLE migrations for new columns (try/except OperationalError pattern) — lxmf_destination_hash, short_name, system_fingerprint were added this way. Same pattern will be used for discovered_via column.

Dashboard screen replaced flat MeshDeviceTable(DataTable) with MeshDeviceTree(Tree) widget that groups discovered devices hierarchically by their discovered_via interface name. Interface branches are auto-expanded, leaf nodes carry device identity as data for selection/navigation.

MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated in StyreneAnnounceHandler.received_announce() by looking up RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5].name — index 5 is the receiving interface object with a .name attribute matching the config stanza name.

NodeStore 'nodes' table has discovered_via TEXT column (ALTER TABLE migration pattern) with idx_discovered_via index. UPSERT uses COALESCE(excluded.discovered_via, nodes.discovered_via) to preserve existing interface info when new announce lacks it.

Hierarchical mesh device tree implemented in dashboard — MeshDeviceTree(Tree) widget replaces flat DataTable, grouping discovered devices under their source interface (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub' branch → child devices, 'Direct / Unknown' → devices without interface info). Uses MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest_hash][5].name post-announce.

NodeStore has 'paths' table with interface_type and interface_name columns per destination_hash. The 'nodes' table now has a discovered_via TEXT column (added via ALTER TABLE migration) with idx_discovered_via index for efficient dashboard Tree grouping. UPSERT uses COALESCE to preserve existing interface info.

DashboardScreen event handling changed from on_data_table_row_selected(DataTable.RowSelected) to on_tree_node_selected(Tree.NodeSelected[str]) for device detail navigation. Tree node .data carries device identity string; None data on branch/empty nodes is ignored.

Dashboard MESH DEVICES panel uses Tree widget (MeshDeviceTree) instead of DataTable as of v0.10.59. Devices grouped by discovered_via interface name. MeshDevice.discovered_via populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5].name in the announce handler (post-hoc lookup — RNS doesn't pass interface to announce callbacks). nodes table has discovered_via column + idx_discovered_via index. COALESCE preserves existing value when re-announce has no interface info.

NodeInfoPanel renders in two-column layout as of v0.10.61. Left column: SYSTEM (CPU/RAM/NET/STORAGE), DAEMON (IPC mode only), IDENTITY (name/alias/hash/PQC tier). Right column: RETICULUM (RNS status/uplink/interfaces), STYRENE (mode/hub/mesh count), VERSION (styrened __version__). Uses Rich markup with regex-based padding for side-by-side rendering within a single Static widget. render() delegates to _render_left_column() and _render_right_column() methods. Located at src/styrened/tui/widgets/node_info_panel.py.

Dashboard panel CSS proportions (v0.10.62): #node-info-panel height:auto max-height:20, #mesh-devices-panel height:2fr min-height:6, #activity-feed-panel height:1fr min-height:4 max-height:16. Mesh devices gets 2/3 remaining vertical space, activity gets 1/3.

HighlightedPanel (Vertical) composes: hp-top Static (1 line) + hp-content Vertical + hp-bottom Static (1 line). hp-content default is height:auto (safe for modals/settings). Dashboard panels (#mesh-devices-panel, #activity-feed-panel) override hp-content to height:1fr via CSS specificity. Box-drawing borders rendered via Rich markup with ColorCascade hex colors.
styrened TUI uses Textual 8.0.0 as of 2026-03-01

Two identity systems coexist: (1) RNS operator identity — cryptographic keypair at reticulum.operator_identity_path, identity hash for routing, (2) Styrene IdentityConfig — display_name, icon, short_name for human-readable appearance. Both stored in core-config.yaml under different sections (reticulum vs identity). Investigation ongoing to ensure they don't conflict.

YubiKey identity provider uses FIDO2 hmac-secret extension to derive deterministic 64-byte RNS identity (X25519 + Ed25519) from hardware token. Two application-specific salts (styrene-encryption-v1, styrene-signing-v1) produce independent 32-byte outputs via getAssertion. Credential ID stored in config as base64. Located at src/styrened/services/yubikey.py. Requires pip install styrened[yubikey] (python-fido2>=1.0).

Identity provider selection in _resolve_identity_path(): priority 0 is YubiKey (if identity_config.provider == 'yubikey'), then config override path, system /etc/styrene/identity, user ~/.config/styrene/identity, LXMF app detection, and finally new generation. YubiKey path calls derive_identity_bytes() and RNS.Identity.from_bytes() inline, returning hex hash directly without writing to disk.

get_operator_identity() and get_operator_identity_object() now delegate to _load_identity_config() which loads IdentityConfig from core-config.yaml, then check provider field. YubiKey provider calls derive_identity_bytes() inline; file provider falls through to _resolve_identity_path() + from_file(). get_operator_identity() wraps get_operator_identity_object() with hash extraction and exception handling.

Well-known RNS community hubs include: dublin.connect.reticulum.network:4965 (Dublin Hub), reticulum.betweentheborders.com:4242 (BetweenTheBorders), istanbul.reserve.network:9034, node01.rns.bnz.se:4242, rns.stoppedcold.com:4242, rtclm.de:4242, sydney.reticulum.au:4242. These are being added alongside rns.styrene.io:4242 as default/selectable peer interfaces.

PeerConfig model now has an 'enabled' field (default True) — parsed from core-config.yaml via _parse_bool(p.get('enabled', True)), serialized as 'enabled' key in _serialize_config(), and used by generate_rns_config() to skip disabled peers (continue if not peer.enabled).

TUI peer rows replaced static status indicator (● dot with CSS color classes) with a Switch toggle (peer_enabled_{i}) that controls the PeerConfig.enabled field. Switch uses .setting-checkbox and .peer-enabled-toggle CSS classes. Peer enabled state persists to core-config.yaml and controls whether the peer is written to ~/.reticulum/config.

WELL_KNOWN_HUBS constant defined in models/config.py — list of 5 PeerConfig entries (Styrene Community Hub enabled, 4 community hubs disabled by default). Used by both daemon (services/config.py) and TUI (tui/services/config.py) config generators to seed new installs.

Config loaders (daemon services/config.py and TUI tui/services/config.py) merge missing WELL_KNOWN_HUBS as disabled entries after parsing peers list. Keyed by (host, port) tuple to avoid duplicates. Existing peers are never modified — only missing hubs are appended with enabled=False. This ensures existing installs see well-known hubs in Settings without manual addition.

MeshDeviceTree CSS changed in latest fix: .tree--cursor background changed from $surface to $background (eliminates visible gray shadow bar on selected row), .tree--highlight changed from $background to transparent (hover no longer shows background change). Selected row identified by $primary color + bold text only.

StyreneConfig.identity is a property that proxies to StyreneConfig.core.identity. The TUI load path calls _overlay_core_identity() which reads core config via load_core_config() and replaces config.core.identity with the loaded IdentityConfig. Settings screen Input widgets are populated from self.config.identity.display_name at compose() time.
No image/media handling exists in StyreneEnvelope wire protocol yet — image attachment support is greenfield. No content_type, attachment, or media fields in models/styrene_wire.py or protocols/.

Wire protocol image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope: MediaAttachment struct with content_type, data, original_type (for lossless JPEG repack tracking), thumbnail (progressive prefix), width, height. Defined in docs/image-format-assessment.md in styrene-rs repo. Vec<MediaAttachment> on envelope.

Image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope finalized: MediaAttachment(content_type, data, original_type, thumbnail, width, height). JXL as native format with JPEG fallback. original_type tracks lossless JPEG repacks for reversible extraction. Target 15-50KB per image. Progressive decode for mesh UX (2KB→1/8 res, 10KB→1/4 res, full). Design doc at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md.

JXL Rust crate ecosystem (2026-03): jxl-oxide 0.12 (pure Rust decoder, active, modular sub-crates), zune-jpegxl 0.5 (pure Rust encoder, early), jxl-encoder 0.1 (pure Rust, early), jpegxl-rs 0.13 (libjxl C bindings). For styrene-mesh, jxl-oxide is primary decode, jpegxl-rs or zune-jpegxl for encode (TBD evaluation).

Python-Rust binding landscape: PyO3 (v0.23+, production-grade, standard choice — used by Polars, ruff, Pydantic V2) + Maturin (v1.8+, build backend for PyO3→wheels) is the clear winner. Also: pyo3-asyncio (Rust futures↔asyncio), rust-numpy (zero-copy ndarray), uniffi (Mozilla multi-lang IDL). Potential future use: styrene-imagecodecs PyO3 crate wrapping jxl-oxide to eliminate libjxl system dep for Python.

JXL lossless JPEG repack flow for Styrene: phone sends JPEG → Styrene wraps to JXL losslessly (20% smaller) with original_type='image/jpeg' → transmit over mesh → receiver can decode JXL or extract bit-exact original JPEG for non-Styrene clients. Zero quality loss, reversible.

Incremental Rust migration strategy via PyO3 FFI proposed in styrene-rs/docs/incremental-rust-migration.md. Two integration modes: (1) wire interop (independent Rust daemon over LXMF), (2) FFI hybrid (Rust modules exposed via PyO3 as styrene-native package, imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements). Uses try/except ImportError pattern for graceful fallback to pure Python.

styrene-native PyO3 crate planned at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ — cdylib extension module built with maturin, re-exports from styrene-mesh/styrene-rns/styrene-lxmf crates. Installed via pip install styrened[native]. Falls back to pure Python when not installed.

Dual-path compatibility verification strategy: pytest fixture with params=['python','rust'] runs every test twice against both implementations. Any behavioral divergence caught immediately. Impossible with wire-only approach. Feature flag STYRENE_NATIVE=0 forces pure Python in production.

styrene-rs has two integration modes with styrened: (1) Wire interop — independent Rust daemon communicates over LXMF mesh (styrened-rs binary), (2) FFI hybrid — Rust modules exposed via PyO3 (styrene-native package) imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements. Wire protocol (StyreneEnvelope in styrene-mesh crate) remains the shared contract for mode 1. Mode 2 enables incremental migration.

styrene-rs PARITY_GAPS.md shows ~37K Rust LOC across 6 crates with 212 tests. Missing service layer (~12K LOC): conversation service, auto-reply, node store persistence, remote terminal, protocol registry, file transfer, hub connection. Critical gaps: IFAC multi-hop bug, Serial/KISS interface, propagation store-and-forward, config system.

styrene-native PyO3 crate scaffolded at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ in styrene-rs repo. Cargo.toml defines cdylib crate type with pyo3 0.23 + extension-module feature, depending on styrene-mesh and styrene-rns path deps. pyproject.toml uses maturin>=1.0 build backend. Package name: styrene-native, lib name: styrene_native.

styrene-mesh crate's wire protocol uses StyreneMessage struct (not StyreneEnvelope) with encode()/decode() methods. Wire format: 10-byte namespace 'styrene.io' + 1-byte version (0x01) + 1-byte type enum + 16-byte request_id + variable msgpack payload. Header is 28 bytes. StyreneMessageType enum covers Control, Status, RPC Commands/Responses, Terminal Sessions, and PQC Sessions ranges.

Python styrened service layer LOC breakdown: reticulum.py 1407, conversation_service.py 1316, lxmf_service.py 1114, config.py 1075, node_store.py 986, doctor.py 753, rns_service.py 653, file_transfer.py 637, auto_reply.py 634, page_browser.py 524, hardware.py 518, pqc_session.py 424, attachment_store.py 359, hub_connection.py 342. Total services ~12.5K LOC. Models total ~17K LOC (styrene_wire.py alone is 1124).

StyreneApp.action_interrupt() implements double ctrl+c quit pattern: single ctrl+c pops screen stack toward dashboard, second ctrl+c within 1.0s window exits app. Uses time.monotonic() tracking via _last_interrupt class var. Binding uses priority=True to bypass focused widget key consumption.

LXMF propagation destination populated in TUI settings from config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination. Community Hub Switch toggle (#community_hub_enabled) auto-fills propagation_destination Input with COMMUNITY_HUB_PROPAGATION_HASH on enable, clears on disable (only if it matches the community hash). Empty propagation field despite enabled hub suggests config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination is None/empty at load time.

TUI config loading changed from _overlay_core_identity() (identity-only) to _overlay_core_config() which replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. This means core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for ALL CoreConfig fields (identity, reticulum, lxmf, rpc, discovery, api). tui.yaml still contains a stale copy of reticulum/rpc/etc sections that gets parsed then overwritten by the overlay.

_overlay_core_config() in tui/services/config.py replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for all CoreConfig fields. Identity is stored in core-config.yaml, settings screen _save_identity() writes there first, then updates self.config.core.identity in memory so subsequent save_core_config() preserves new values.

MeshDeviceTree does NOT filter LOST nodes — all device statuses (ACTIVE, STALE, LOST) are displayed with different status symbols (● active, ◐ stale, ○ lost). Previous DataTable implementation filtered LOST nodes out.
Non-human entities shall not receive author or collaborator credit - no Co-Authored-By trailers for AI tools in git commits

styrened is adopting full authority as the primary interface for Reticulum configuration - the TUI Network tab will become a proper Reticulum interface manager for TCPClientInterface peers, AutoInterface toggle, and transport mode

Settings Network tab redesigned (2026-03-01): Replaced vestigial Hub selector (LXMF propagation layer) with proper Reticulum interface manager — Peers list (TCPClientInterface), AutoInterface toggle, Server interface, Transport mode. Save writes both core-config.yaml and regenerates ~/.reticulum/config. Hub LXMF fields (hub_enabled, hub_address, hub_announce_interval) remain in CoreConfig but are no longer exposed in settings UI.

styrene-pypi dependency on styrened was changed to ~=0.10 compatible release specifier to fix publish race condition, but this caused pipx upgrade to not pull newer styrened (0.10.40 satisfies ~=0.10). The sync-version.yml workflow uses >=X.Y.Z pins which are semantically correct but require the workflow to run after styrened publishes. Both approaches have tradeoffs being resolved.
styrene-pypi sync-version.yml cron changed from every 6 hours to hourly during active development period

Announce interval changed from raw numeric Input to Select widget with 14 human-readable presets (15s through 1d). Uses _match_announce_interval() helper to map current config value to nearest preset. ANNOUNCE_INTERVALS constant defined at module level.

TUI layout redesign underway: new CSS class hierarchy (.setting-input, .setting-input-narrow, .setting-select, .setting-checkbox) ensures widget width is proportional to semantic content size. Labels fixed-width right-aligned at 22 chars. This establishes the pattern before any Rust/ratatui port.

Announce interval UI now uses Select widget with 14 preset options (15s, 30s, 45s, 1m, 2m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 1d) via ANNOUNCE_INTERVALS constant. Replaced raw numeric Input widget. Uses _match_announce_interval() to find nearest preset for current config value.

TUI replaced all Checkbox widgets with Switch widgets across settings screens (v0.10.52) — Textual Switch renders as proper sliding toggle instead of X-in-a-box character. All query_one/query calls updated from Checkbox to Switch.

Hierarchical mesh device tree implemented: MeshDevice.discovered_via populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest_hash][5].name post-announce. Dashboard uses Textual Tree widget with devices grouped under interface branches (named interfaces sorted alphabetically, 'Direct / Unknown' last). Tree leaf data carries device identity for selection/detail navigation.

Default peer config being expanded from just Styrene Community Hub (rns.styrene.io:4242) to include well-known upstream RNS community hubs. Operators on first launch should see Styrene hub plus ability to see/choose from well-known shared interfaces.

UpgradeScreen replaced HighlightedPanel with plain bordered Vertical container in v0.10.74 — HighlightedPanel's custom border Statics (hp-top/hp-bottom) are fundamentally incompatible with ModalScreen overlay contexts. Uses native Textual border:solid $panel, centered Static title, background:$surface.

JXL (JPEG XL) accepted as native Styrene image format. Key factors: best compression at ≤50KB (mesh sweet spot), lossless JPEG repack (unique — 20% smaller, bit-exact reversible), progressive decode for slow links, pure Rust decoder (jxl-oxide 0.12, actively maintained), clean BSD-3 license. WebP rejected (less efficient at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, pure Rust zenwebp only 0.3). AVIF rejected (patent complexity, 3x slower ARM decode, fragmented Rust crates). JPEG accepted as universal fallback.

Image format alternatives assessment completed and documented at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md. Rejected: HEIF (patents, no Rust), AVIF (patent complexity, slow ARM decode, fragmented Rust), QOI (worse than JPEG at ≤50KB), FLIF (dead), BPG (dead, H.265 patents), WebP (not best at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, less mature pure Rust). WebP and JPEG remain accepted receive formats.

PyO3 hybrid daemon approach accepted to supersede 'no FFI, no PyO3 bindings' stance. Enables incremental module-by-module migration from Python to Rust within the running styrened daemon, with per-module compatibility verification via dual-path test fixtures (same tests run against both Python and Rust implementations).

Rust migration phased: Phase 1 (data layer, no RNS coupling) — styrene_wire.py, node_store.py, mesh_device.py, conversation_service.py. Phase 2 (crypto/protocol) — pqc_session.py, file_transfer.py, rns_service.py. Phase 3 (RNS integration) — reticulum.py, lxmf_service.py. Never port: TUI, config, doctor, CLI, auto_reply.

styrene-rs structural decisions documented: (S1) Replace Rc<RpcDaemon> with Arc for multi-threaded tokio runtime — Mutex fields already Send+Sync, only Rc prevents it. (S2) Extract MeshTransport trait from concrete 500+ LOC Transport struct for testability and backend swapping.
Network settings changes require daemon restart to take effect - the RNS config is regenerated on save but the running Reticulum instance is not reloaded
GitHub Dependabot found 1 high-severity vulnerability on styrened's default branch (as of 2026-03-01)

TUI Network tab peer rows allocate disproportionate space to host/IP field while peer name is truncated — community hub label (e.g., rns.styrene.io) appears as truncated gross label despite available real estate

Identity at ~/.config/styrene/identity is separate from RNS transport identity in ~/.reticulum/storage/. The upgrade path (pipx upgrade + pkill daemon) does NOT touch identity files. User-reported identity loss on upgrade needs investigation — may be related to ~/.reticulum/config regeneration causing RNS storage directory recreation

Users may get a new RNS transport identity upon upgrade to v0.10.42+. Operator identity (~/.config/styrene/identity) is NOT affected by upgrade. The upgrade path (pipx upgrade styrene + pkill daemon) doesn't touch config/identity. Possible cause: config save regenerating ~/.reticulum/config which may trigger RNS storage recreation on restart. Needs investigation.

TUI Network tab had CSS rendering bugs: v0.10.40 port/remove-btn truncated (fixed with wider min-widths), v0.10.42 peer name truncated at 20 chars (fixed in v0.10.43 by switching to proportional 2fr sizing and adding column headers)

styrene-pypi publish workflow has a race condition: smoke test does pip install of the wheel which requires styrened>=X.Y.Z from PyPI, but styrened hasn't been published yet by Argo CI. All styrene-pypi releases after 0.10.40 failed (0.10.41-0.10.44) because of this.

TUI upgrade restart implemented via os.execvp in _restart_tui() method (v0.10.44) — finds styrene entry point and replaces current process. Uses atexit handler to exec after Textual event loop teardown. However, upgrade itself fails because styrene-pypi is stuck at 0.10.40 on PyPI.

styrene-pypi publish race condition (fixed 2026-03-01): Meta-package was pinning `styrened>=X.Y.Z` with exact version, but its GitHub Actions publish ran before the Argo styrened publish completed. The smoke test failed because styrened wasn't on PyPI yet. Fixed by using `~=0.10` compatible release specifier instead of exact version floor.

pipx upgrade styrene with ~=0.10 specifier doesn't upgrade styrened because pip's default --upgrade-strategy=only-if-needed sees existing 0.10.40 as satisfying the constraint. Fix: _build_upgrade_cmd() now passes --pip-args='--upgrade-strategy=eager' to force transitive dep upgrades.

pipx upgrade styrene to 0.10.45 upgrades the meta-package but leaves styrened at 0.10.40 in the venv — pip's default --upgrade-strategy=only-if-needed doesn't pull transitive deps when the constraint (~=0.10) is already satisfied. The eager strategy fix in 0.10.45 is a catch-22: users need 0.10.45 installed to get the fix that would have installed 0.10.45.

on_add_peer mounted new peer rows inside Add Peer button's parent Horizontal instead of hp-content Vertical, causing horizontal stacking — fixed in v0.10.47 by mounting into add_btn_row.parent before the button row

TUI Settings Network tab peer row horizontal stacking bug (delete+re-add) was caused by on_add_peer mounting into wrong container (button's parent Horizontal instead of hp-content Vertical) — fixed in v0.10.47

pipx upgrade --pip-args passed as two separate list elements ('--pip-args', '--upgrade-strategy=eager') instead of single combined arg ('--pip-args=--upgrade-strategy=eager'), causing pipx to not apply eager strategy — fix in progress for v0.10.47+

styrene-pypi sync-version.yml created GitHub releases via GITHUB_TOKEN which can't trigger other workflows (GitHub anti-cascade protection). This broke the release→publish event chain. Textual TUI black bar root cause (fixed v0.10.54): Zero global scrollbar styling existed in imperial_crt.tcss. Every scrollable widget (Log, RichLog, VerticalScroll, overflow-y:scroll) fell through to Textual's built-in defaults which render scrollbar tracks as opaque black. Fix: global Screen scrollbar rules + blanket transparent background on all scrollable widget types + RichLog/Log background:transparent to inherit from parent chain.

pipx upgrade doesn't upgrade transitive deps by default. pipx upgrade styrene upgrades the meta-package but styrened stays at old version because pip's --upgrade-strategy=only-if-needed sees existing version as satisfying ~=0.10. Fix baked into styrened 0.10.48+: _build_upgrade_cmd() uses --pip-args=--upgrade-strategy=eager (single string, NOT two separate args). Users on pre-0.10.48 need one-time: pipx runpip styrene install --upgrade --upgrade-strategy=eager styrened

TUI first-run config (tui/services/config.py) had hardcoded 192.168.0.102 LAN IP for community hub peer instead of rns.styrene.io. Fixed in v0.10.49. The daemon config (services/config.py) already had the correct public hostname. Both must be kept in sync when default peer config changes.

Textual 8.0 key binding pattern: Screen-level bindings that must fire regardless of focused child widget need priority=True on the Binding. Without it, focused widgets (Tree, Input, etc.) consume keys before they bubble to Screen even if the widget has no handler for that key.
